answer_1.quote: To probe which types of LLM-generated outputs (system behaviors) participants might deem to be human-like, and how they would rewrite those outputs to make them less human-like...
answer_1.outputs: The paper studies anthropomorphic behaviors in text generated by LLMs in conversational settings and interventions to make such outputs less human-like.

answer_4.quote: We recruited a total of 350 US-based, English-speaking participants on Prolific, with each participant completing a single task that included four different examples (pairs of user input and generated responses).
answer_4.guideline: Participants were asked to highlight words or phrases that seem human-like, rate how human-like the text appears on a five-point scale, select why the text appears human-like from a multiple-choice list, answer an open-ended question about other human-like qualities, and rewrite the text to be less human-like.
